description: Starter model catalog for MMIR.ai. Static guidance only. Verify exact model tags, availability, license terms and pricing with the selected backend/provider before production use.

models.label: Custom / user supplied
models.notes: Use this when the model is selected inside a trusted backend such as Open WebUI, Ollama or a custom MMIR-compatible connector.

models.label: Llama family
models.best_for: General chat, RAG, agents, instruction following, multi-model reasoning
models.ram_hint: small variants may run on modest RAM; larger variants require high RAM/VRAM
models.gpu_hint: recommended for larger variants and higher throughput
models.cpu_hint: possible for small/quantized variants, slower on larger models
models.notes: Strong general open-weight family. Capacity, license terms and commercial constraints depend on exact model/version.

models.label: Gemma family
models.best_for: General chat, lightweight reasoning, local tests, constrained deployments
models.ram_hint: good candidate for lower-cost local or VM setups depending on tag
models.gpu_hint: optional for smaller variants; useful for speed
models.cpu_hint: small/quantized variants can be tested on CPU
models.notes: Good first test family for local/Ollama-style backends. Verify exact tag, terms and hardware.

models.label: Mistral family
models.provider_family: Mistral AI / open and hosted ecosystem
models.best_for: Fast chat, practical assistants, European provider options
models.ram_hint: small variants may fit standard local/VM capacity; larger variants need more RAM/VRAM
models.gpu_hint: recommended for larger or high-throughput use
models.notes: Often useful when speed and practical assistant behavior matter. Verify license and commercial rights per exact model.

models.label: Qwen family
models.best_for: Multilingual tasks, coding, general assistants, tool use experiments
models.ram_hint: varies widely by size; larger models require high RAM/VRAM
models.gpu_hint: recommended for coding/reasoning variants and high throughput
models.notes: Good candidate for multilingual and coding-heavy MMIR use cases. Verify exact model license and requirements.

models.label: DeepSeek family
models.best_for: Reasoning, coding, technical tasks, analysis workflows
models.ram_hint: distilled variants may run on smaller setups; larger reasoning models need significant capacity
models.gpu_hint: recommended for useful latency and larger variants
models.cpu_hint: small distilled variants may work on CPU but can be slow
models.notes: Useful candidate for technical and reasoning workflows. Verify exact tags, model card, license and hardware needs per backend.

models.label: Phi family
models.best_for: Small local tasks, fast prototyping, constrained VMs
models.ram_hint: good candidate for constrained local/VM setups
models.cpu_hint: good candidate for CPU/local testing depending on tag
models.notes: Candidate for low-cost or low-capacity backends. Verify exact license and model card before commercial use.

models.label: Code-specialist models
models.best_for: Programming, repo analysis, code generation, refactoring
models.ram_hint: varies widely by model and quantization
models.cpu_hint: possible for smaller code models but may be slow
models.context_hint: longer context is useful for repository work
models.notes: Use a backend-specific code model tag or a hosted coding model. License must be checked per model.

models.label: Embedding models
models.best_for: Vector search, document retrieval, RAG source indexing
models.ram_hint: usually lighter than chat models, but corpus size affects infrastructure
models.cpu_hint: often suitable for CPU batch/indexing depending on volume
models.context_hint: depends on embedding model and chunking strategy
models.notes: Not a chat model by itself. Used to power search and retrieval for RAG.

models.label: Vision / multimodal models
models.best_for: Image understanding, screenshots, diagrams, multimodal workflows
models.cpu_hint: limited practicality except for small variants
models.notes: Useful later for image, document and UI analysis. Requires backend support and model-specific license checks.

models.label: Paid frontier API model
models.best_for: Highest-quality reasoning, multimodal tasks, production assistants
models.notes: Must be accessed through a protected backend/router. Do not expose provider keys in GitHub Pages.

capacity_profiles.label: Low
capacity_profiles.description: Small local model, constrained VM, low cost, lower throughput.

capacity_profiles.label: Standard
capacity_profiles.description: Default CPU or modest accelerated backend for general chat.

capacity_profiles.label: GPU Small
capacity_profiles.description: Small GPU or hosted accelerated instance for faster tokens and larger context.

capacity_profiles.label: GPU Large
capacity_profiles.description: Larger GPU capacity for heavier models, multiple users or high throughput.

capacity_profiles.label: Provider hosted
capacity_profiles.description: SaaS/API model where provider handles GPU capacity. Keep API keys server-side.

capacity_profiles.label: Auto / future router
capacity_profiles.description: Future MMIR router chooses backend and capacity policy automatically.
